body:
20 Nov 2026, P2-25 SLICE 4, PR #118 FIX ROUND (built, not walked, not deployed; P2-25 stays todo; B-46 is item N-46). Replaces my first note of this round (its cost sentence was too rosy). An earlier attempt of this round died in the shutdown with half-built code (saved outside the tree); this is the finished round, on top of main (#120 merged in: docs only).

RULE (lead, 17 Nov): a wrong move is worse than none.
1 A file is re-pointed only when its current ref does NOT also fit it (refs.names_ref: any plausible answer of any tier of candidates, or its own key is the tags' key whatever its length says). Else the file stays, the ref stays on the worklist, one line with ids. The LAST file of a song a person owns never moves (ref_janitor.owned_by_people = the janitor's POINTERS minus the files; asked in the write transaction). The reviewer's case (like on R, duplicate X holds the ISRC) no longer strands the like; the glued-different-song case still moves. The three id columns are unique indexes, so the ids tier cannot hide the current ref; only the length filter of the name tier could: closed.
WHAT FREES A HELD REF (docs/18, RELEASE-CANDIDATE 4b, CHANGELOG, design, module, audit text now say it per kind): no usable tags or placeholder artist with no id = the Host tags or removes the file. A song that fits as well as another (R has no ISRC, X holds the one the tags carry) = tagging CANNOT help (the tags are right) and R and X share no file so refmerge never folds them: only removing the file or taking the ISRC out of its tags; otherwise HELD FOR GOOD. Same name, another length = R's stored length corrected, or the file removed. Last file of an owned song = the song gains another file.
2 The old song prefers a file judged kept or a keeper's, never one nobody could judge (end of the pass, from ref_recheck.moved; phones told).
3 DECIDED AT THE SOURCE: the prune no longer treats a LISTED file with unreadable tags as gone (seen_ids). Through link_library its row was pruned and its ref released: the opposite of docs/18. THIS CHANGES THE PRUNE FOR EVERY REF (no test pinned the old behaviour). rekey_audit now names the files (row id, music server id, song id).
4 Failure guard in finish(): test added; deleting the guard turns 3 tests red.
5 Release paced, 500 rows per transaction (RELEASE_CHUNK). 200,000 synthetic refs: old = ONE transaction, lock held 1,091 ms (3.0 s on a busy machine); new = 400 transactions, longest 6 ms, whole release 6.65 s instead of 1.17 s (each transaction opens a connection). begin() reads every row: 1.15 s, 114 MB, a read, unchanged. The merge it owes is a durable debt (setting rehome_merge_owed, written with the first release, cleared only when refmerge.repair ran and did not fail), retried at the NEXT pass.
6 A pass that ends with nothing to do, or finds the worklist empty, spends the pending copy record (repair_copy.settle, rehome.idle).

PROOF: tests first, seen red on the merged head (23 red); 21 mutations red; whole suite 2616 passed, 13 skipped, 1 xfailed; ruff, format, mypy, check_rows, check_order clean. Copy of VM 108's DB (sha256 1d26a5f77d6dbd7a, 11,784,192 bytes, unchanged): 12 library refs forced on the worklist, 12 kept, 0 moved, every table identical but the worklist; audit_stack check rekey PASS.

FOR THE LEAD: (a) N-36's trigger is an empty worklist on every install, so a ref held for good (above) means it never fires on that Host: does N-36 need a rule for refs held by design? (b) the prune change in 3; (c) the 6.65 s release at 200,000 refs (one constant). NOT DONE: the walk, any deploy, audit_stack check library on a real stack.
